title: World models that preserve decisions and interventions
objective: Determine what additional structure beyond predictive latent agreement can make a compact world representation identifiable for actions and sufficient for a specified decision problem.
deliverables: A comparison of predictive, action-conditioned, causal, and decision-sufficient representation objectives
An explicit pair of observationally indistinguishable environments with different action consequences
A proposed sufficient condition or impossibility statement with a proof attempt
A minimal intervention-based experiment and compact-architecture candidate, both labeled proposed
A source-backed novelty assessment and go-or-park decision
success_criteria: The representation target, action coverage, observability, and identifiability equivalence are explicit
The report distinguishes lower prediction loss from better downstream decisions
Any compactness claim counts encoders, memory, planning, data, and rollout costs
The proposal is compared with the closest primary work rather than presented as a generic replacement for JEPA
stop_conditions: The assignment or round budget is exhausted
The desired guarantee requires unavailable interventions or untestable assumptions; report this boundary
No distinction from prior work survives review
The claimed sufficiency is disproved by a concrete environment pair
